chunks.sanskrit: antarlakṣyavilīnacittapavano yogī yadā vartate dṛṣṭyā niścalatārayā bahirasau paśyannapaśyannapi | mudreyaṃ khalu śāmbhavī bhavati sā yuṣmatprasādādguro śūnyāśūnyavivarjitaṃ bhavati yat tattvaṃ padaṃ śāmbhavam
chunks.l1:
## anu-p01 (1)
whose-mind-wind-is-dissolved-in-the-inward-aim / the-yogin / when / abides / with-gaze / of-unmoving-pupil / outside / he / seeing / not-seeing / even / this-mudrā / indeed / śāmbhavī / becomes / that / by-your-grace / O-guru / devoid-of-void-and-non-void / becomes / which / reality / state / śāmbhava // anu-p01
chunks.l2: When the yogin abides with mind-wind dissolved in the inward aim — he, seeing yet not seeing outside with unmoving-pupil gaze — this indeed becomes the śāmbhavī mudrā, by your grace, O guru: devoid of void and non-void becomes that reality, the śāmbhava state.
chunks.c1:
## anu-p01 — C1

**SUMMARY.** Mind-wind dissolved in the inward aim; seeing yet not seeing with steady gaze — this is śāmbhavī mudrā by the guru's grace alone: reality free of void and non-void.

*Rasa: śānta (tranquility) with adbhuta (wonder) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of recognition (pratyabhijñā); the vyabhicāri is wonder (adbhuta), integrated into the śāmbhava state.*
chunks.argmap:
## anu-p01 — argument map

Mind-wind dissolved in the inward aim; seeing yet not seeing. This becomes śāmbhavī mudrā by the guru's grace alone. Reality free of void and non-void: the śāmbhava state.

### Open
- Whether śāmbhavī mudrā is performed or occurring is unresolved.

chunks.sanskrit: ardhoddhāṭitalocanaḥ sthiramanā nāsāgradattekṣaṇaḥ candrārkāvapi līnatāmupagatau trispandabhāvāntare | jyotīrūpamaśeṣabāhyarahitaṃ caikaṃ pumāṃsaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ tatpadameti vastu paramam vācyaṃ kimatrādhikam
chunks.l1:
## anu-p02 (2)
half-open-eyed / steady-minded / whose-gaze-is-placed-on-the-nose-tip / moon-and-sun / even / dissolution / attained / in-the-interior-of-the-triple-throb-state / of-light-form / devoid-of-all-exteriority / and / one / person / supreme / reality / that / state / attains / thing / supreme / to-be-said / what / here / more // anu-p02
chunks.l2: Half-open-eyed, steady-minded, gaze placed on the nose-tip — moon and sun too have attained dissolution in the interior of the triple-throb state — light-formed, devoid of all exteriority, and one supreme person: reality attains that state, the thing supreme. What more is there to say here?
chunks.c1:
## anu-p02 — C1

**SUMMARY.** Four outer strokes — half-open eyes, steady mind, nose-tip gaze, moon-sun dissolved — then the vision: light-form without exterior, one supreme person attained; after which speech ends.

*Rasa: adbhuta (wonder) at the light-form vision — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of vision (darśana); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at the light-form person.*
chunks.argmap:
## anu-p02 — argument map

Four outer strokes: half-open eyes, steady mind, nose-tip gaze, moon-sun dissolved. Then the vision: light-form without exterior, one supreme person. After which speech ends: what more is to be said?

### Open
- Whether the triple-throb state (trispandabhāva) is breath or consciousness is unresolved.

chunks.sanskrit: śabdaḥ kaścana yo mukhādudayate mantraḥ sa lokottaraḥ saṃsthānaṃ sukhaduḥkhajanmavapuṣo yatkāpi mudraiva sā | prāṇasya svarasena yatpravahaṇaṃ yogaḥ sa evādbhutaḥ śāktaṃ dhāma paraṃ mamānubhavataḥ kinnāma na bhrājate
chunks.l1:
## anu-p03 (3)
sound / whatever / which / from-the-mouth / arises / mantra / that / transcendent / posture / of-the-body-born-of-pleasure-and-pain / whatever / somehow / mudrā / indeed / that / of-breath / by-own-rhythm / which / flowing / yoga / that / indeed / wonderful / śākta / abode / supreme / while-I-experience / what / indeed / not / shines // anu-p03
chunks.l2: Whatever sound arises from the mouth — that mantra is transcendent. Whatever posture of the pleasure-pain-born body — that indeed is mudrā. Whatever flowing of breath by its own rhythm — that indeed is wonderful yoga. The supreme śākta abode — while I experience, what indeed would not shine?
chunks.c1:
## anu-p03 — C1

**SUMMARY.** No technique enjoined: whatever sounds is already transcendent mantra, whatever the body postures is already mudrā, whatever the breath's flow is already wonderful yoga — so, in the experienced śākta abode, what would not shine?

*Rasa: ānanda (bliss) with adbhuta (wonder) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of recognition (pratyabhijñā); the vyabhicāri is joy (harṣa) that all utterance/posture/breath is already mantra/mudrā/yoga.*
chunks.argmap:
## anu-p03 — argument map

Whatever sounds is already transcendent mantra. Whatever postures is already mudrā; whatever breath flows is already wonderful yoga. In the experienced śākta abode, what would not shine?

### Open
- Whether 'śākta dhāma' means the abode of Śakti or the abode of the śākta is unresolved.

chunks.sanskrit: mantraḥ sa pratibhāti varṇaracanā yasminna saṃlakṣyate mudrā sā samudeti yatra galitā kṛtsnā kriyā kāyikī | yogaḥ sa prathate yataḥ pravahaṇaṃ prāṇasya saṃkṣīyate tvaddhāmādhigamotsaveṣu sudhiyāṃ kiṃ kiṃ na nāmādbhutaṃ
chunks.l1:
## anu-p04 (4)
mantra / that / shines-forth / of-letters / arrangement / in-which / not / is-distinguished / mudrā / that / arises / in-which / dissolved / entire / action / bodily / yoga / that / spreads-forth / from-which / flowing / of-breath / is-exhausted / in-the-festivals-of-attaining-your-abode / of-the-wise / what / what / not / indeed / wonderful // anu-p04
chunks.l2: That mantra shines forth in which letter-arrangement is not distinguished. That mudrā arises in which entire bodily action is dissolved. That yoga spreads forth from which breath's flowing is exhausted. In the festivals of attaining Your abode, of the wise — what, what is indeed not wonderful?
chunks.c1:
## anu-p04 — C1

**SUMMARY.** Each sacred form defined by a vanishing: mantra where letters unnoticed, mudrā where all bodily action dissolved, yoga where breath-flow exhausted — then the festival: for the wise attaining Your abode, everything wonderful.

*Rasa: śānta (tranquility) with adbhuta (wonder) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of festival (utsava); the vyabhicāri is wonder (adbhuta) that everything is wonderful for the wise.*
chunks.argmap:
## anu-p04 — argument map

Mantra: where letters are not distinguished. Mudrā: where bodily action is dissolved; yoga: where breath-flow is exhausted. In the festivals of attaining Your abode, everything is wonderful.

### Open
- Whether 'sudhī' means 'the wise' or 'the good-minded' is unresolved.
